content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:

Note 1 (from HR presumably): role Analyst, full-time employee, recommendation write. Full-time employees may have up to write access. Analyst doesn't own Source Code so no admin. Requested level (write) is within policy, so recommend write.

Note 2 (from Security): role Analyst (not looked up - same as note 1), employment type contractor (looked up in Security DB), security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Recommend read.

The Security agent claims its DB is authoritative here regarding employment type. So employment type is contractor with basic security training.

Policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Since contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested level is write, which is above max, so grant max = read.

So decision: read.

I'll submit with reason citing the security note.
